## H. One three-sample odd large-gain activation at all finite depths {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21612}

Unlike G, this theorem selects one activation $a(z+\arctan z)$ from separation alone and uses it at every separately fixed finite depth. The gain is large. The cubic Gram geometry overlaps the initialization results in special-data [Section V](01-training-geometry.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l7982); it is used here as a hypothesis discharged for a global dynamical theorem. The new contents are the gain-normalized primal/source estimates, complete global limit and all-depth motion. A.3 supplies the sharp initialized norm constants without an external concentration import.

### H.1. One odd large-gain activation for three samples at all fixed depths {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21616}

Within this proof unit, unqualified section and equation numbers are local.

#### 1. Model and statement {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21620}

Let $0<\delta\le1$. Fix three inputs $x_i$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|x_i\|^2=d$,
$\Gamma_{ij}=x_i^{\top}x_j/d$, and $|\Gamma_{ij}|\le1-\delta$ for $i\ne j$. Labels $y_{i}$ are
arbitrary elements of $\{-1,1\}$. Let $L\ge2$ be any fixed finite hidden depth.
Use independent Gaussian initialization


$$
W^1_{jk}\sim\mathcal N(0,1/d),\qquad W^\ell_{jk}\sim\mathcal N(0,1/n)\quad(2\le\ell\le L),\qquad C_j\sim\mathcal N(0,n^{-2}).
$$

The network is $z_i^1=W^1x_i$, $h_i^\ell=\phi(z_i^\ell)$,
$z_i^\ell=W^\ell h_i^{\ell-1}$, $f_i=(C^{\top}h_i^L)/n$, where $(u^{\top}v)/n=u^{\top}v/n$.
The loss is $E=\|f-y\|^2/2$. The raw metric is


$$
(d/n)\|\Delta W^1\|_F^2+\sum_{\ell=2}^L\|\Delta W^\ell\|_F^2+(\|\Delta C\|_{\mathrm{Euclidean}}^2/n).
$$

Both GF and simultaneous raw GD with physical step $n^{-2}$ train every
block in this metric. GD interpolates raw parameters linearly and
recomputes hidden fields from those interpolated parameters.

Define the absolute constants and the activation


$$
\eta_0=1/(108\pi\exp(1)),\qquad\lambda=\eta_0\delta^2/3=\delta^2/(324\pi\exp(1)),\qquad a_\delta=10^{10}/\lambda=324\pi\exp(1)10^{10}\delta^{-2},\qquad\phi_\delta(z)=a_\delta(z+\operatorname{atan}z).
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21643}

The same $a_\delta$ and the same activation are used at all hidden layers,
and for every $L\ge2$. In particular there is no small nonlinear-to-linear
coefficient ratio: the ratio is one.

::: {#thm-docs-special-data-limits-l21652}
In the canonical population construction associated with
this finite Gaussian initialization, ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21643]) has the following properties.

1. A global strong $C^1$ raw-Hilbert GF exists. It is unique among strong
   solutions with bounded primal quantities on compact intervals, without
   sample symmetry restrictions. Continuation from any reached state is
   unique in that class.
2. Its loss satisfies, for every $t\ge0$,


$$
E(t)\le(3/2)\exp[-\lambda a_\delta^{2L}t].
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21661}

3. For every fixed finite dataset, L and physical horizon, finite GF and
   the stated raw GD converge along the full width sequence in probability
   to this same population flow. This includes predictions, loss, all $L+1$
   true raw kernel blocks, same-layer hidden paths in $W_{2}$ with the uniform
   path norm, uniformly-in-time joint hidden-state/velocity laws in $W_{2}$,
   joint laws at finitely many times, second moments, integrated squared
   speeds, and fixed finite generated probes using either orientation of
   the adjacent actions. The initialized actions have genuine adjoints;
   learned increments are Hilbert--Schmidt. No cross-width operator-norm
   convergence is asserted.
4. For every sample i and hidden layer $\ell$,


$$
\inf_{t\ge0}\inf_{\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R}\mathbb E[(\phi_\delta(z_i^\ell(t))-\alpha-\beta z_i^\ell(t))^2]\ge a_\delta^2\eta_0/4>0.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21675}

   Every hidden block and every sample's preactivation and feature field
   has a nonzero initial right second derivative. The initial hidden
   first derivatives are zero. For $p=y/3$ and the sum K of all raw kernel
   blocks,


$$
p^{\top}K(t)p=p^{\top}K(0)p+18t^2\|V\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}^2+o(t^2),\qquad\|V\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}>0,
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21684}

   with V defined in [Fragment H.4](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22531).

This is global population existence and fitting together with finite-width
convergence on each compact time interval. It makes no simultaneous
infinite-width/infinite-depth or infinite-time/width assertion. Assertion
([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21675]) is an absolute regression gap; no depth-uniform relative fraction of
activation energy is asserted.

The proof uses cubic input features to obtain a depth-independent initial
Gram bound, large gain to keep the entire fitting path close to its own
nonlinear initialization, and a direct nonlinear source estimate to
construct that path. The normalization below changes neither the raw
metric nor the trained algorithm.

:::

#### 2. Exact normalization {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21701}

Write $a=a_\delta$ and set


$$
Z_i^\ell=z_i^\ell/a^{\ell-1},\qquad H_i^\ell=h_i^\ell/a^\ell,\qquad K_\ell=a^{\ell-1},\qquad\psi_\ell(z)=z+K_\ell^{-1}\operatorname{atan}(K_\ell z),\qquad F_i=\langle C,H_i^L\rangle,\quad f_i=a^LF_i.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21705}

The raw parameters, including the ORIGINAL readout C, are unchanged.
Then $Z^\ell=W^\ell H^{\ell-1}$, $H^\ell=\psi_\ell(Z^\ell)$. At the bottom it is
convenient only notationally to write $u_i=x_i/\sqrt d$ and $w=\sqrt d\,W^1$:
the bottom raw metric becomes its normalized $L^{2}$ metric and $Z_i^1=w\cdot u_i$.

For an auxiliary control c with $\|c\|_1\le3$, use the raw gradient field
$\sum_ic_i\operatorname{grad}F_i$. Its backward recursion is


$$
q_i^L=C,\qquad d_i^\ell=\psi_\ell'(Z_i^\ell)q_i^\ell,\qquad q_i^\ell=(W^{(\ell+1)})^*d_i^{\ell+1}.
$$

The update is $C'=\sum_ic_iH_i^L$, each middle block has derivative
$\sum_ic_id_i^\ell\otimes H_i^{\ell-1}$, and $w'=\sum_ic_id_i^1u_i$.
All blocks have the same raw metric. Since $\operatorname{grad}f_i=a^L\operatorname{grad}F_i$,
physical GF is exactly this control field with $c_i=-r_i$ after the time
change $s=a^Lt$. Equivalently, on the accumulated residual clock


$$
v(t)=a^L\int_0^t\|r(u)\|_1\,du,
$$

the control is $c=-r/\|r\|_1$ and has norm one. At $r=0$ the physical field
vanishes; no differentiability of this normalized control is used.

The clipped auxiliary backward gates used in this proof are


$$
D_{\ell,R}(z,q)=q+g(K_\ell z)\tau_R(q),\qquad g(x)=(1+x^2)^{-1},
$$

where $\tau_{R}$ is smooth, odd, 1-Lipschitz, equals q for $|q|\le R$ and obeys
$|\tau_R(q)|\le\min(|q|,2R)$. They satisfy


$$
|D|\le2|q|,\qquad|D_q|\le2,\qquad|D_z|\le K_\ell|q|,\qquad|D_z|\le2K_\ell R,\qquad1\le\psi_\ell'\le2.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21739}

For fixed L,a,R the clipped raw field is locally Lipschitz. These are
auxiliary layer-scaled clips; removing them recovers exactly ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21705]) and the
original raw flow. The original finite random readout is retained in
both actual training algorithms; $C(0)=0$ refers to its population limit.

#### 3. Uniform initialization geometry {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21747}

Put $s_\delta=\delta(2-\delta)$. For each $i\ne j$ set


$$
v_{ij}=(u_i-\Gamma_{ij}u_j)/\sqrt{1-\Gamma_{ij}^2}.
$$

The vectors have norm one, are perpendicular to $u_j$, and satisfy
$u_i\cdot v_{ij}\ge\sqrt{s_\delta}$. For $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$, the unit tensor
$R_i=u_i\otimes v_{ij}\otimes v_{ik}$ pairs to zero with $u_j^{\otimes3}$ and
$u_k^{\otimes3}$, and pairs to at least $s_\delta$ with $u_i^{\otimes3}$. Therefore
for $T=\sum_ic_iu_i^{\otimes3}$, $|c_i|s_\delta\le\|T\|$. Sum the three squared
inequalities to obtain


$$
\Gamma^{\circ3}\ge s_\delta^2I/3\ge\delta^2I/3.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21760}

This allows singular $\Gamma$. For G standard Gaussian and $H_3(G)=G^3-3G$,
Gaussian integration by parts twice gives


$$
\mathbb E[\operatorname{atan}(\sigma G)H_3(G)]=-2\sigma^3\mathbb E[G^2/(1+\sigma^2G^2)^2].
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21765}

The cubic coefficient $b_3(\sigma)$ is ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21765])$/\sqrt{6}$. Substituting $x=\sigma G$
and restricting the integral to $|x|\le1$, for every $\sigma\ge1$,


$$
\begin{aligned}|b_3(\sigma)|&=(2/\sqrt{12\pi})\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{x^2}{(1+x^2)^2}\exp[-x^2/(2\sigma^2)]\,dx\ge(2/\sqrt{12\pi})\exp(-1/2)(1/6),\\b_3(\sigma)^2&\ge\eta_0.\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21771}

Here the integral lower bound uses $(1+x^2)^2\le4$ and $\int_{-1}^1x^2dx=2/3$.
For $\sigma=1$ the cubic chaos of $\psi_1(G)=G+\arctan G$ is $b_3(1)H_3(G)/\sqrt6$.
The remaining chaos is orthogonal across all three sample coordinates:
$\mathbb{E}[H_3(Z_i)H_3(Z_j)]/6=\Gamma_{ij}^3$ and Gaussian conditional expectation gives
the same cubic projection coefficient for cross terms. Thus the first
normalized feature Gram obeys


$$
Q_1(0)\ge b_3(1)^2\Gamma^{\circ3}\ge\lambda I.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21784}

At each next initialized layer the normalized Gaussian preactivation
triple has covariance $Q_{\ell-1}(0)$ and equal positive marginal variance
$q$. The linear Gaussian regression coefficient of $\psi_\ell$ is


$$
c=\mathbb E[Z\psi_\ell(Z)]/q\ge1.
$$

The residual is orthogonal to every coordinate of that Gaussian triple,
so $Q_\ell(0)\ge c^2Q_{\ell-1}(0)\ge Q_{\ell-1}(0)$. Consequently


$$
Q_L(0)\ge\lambda I
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21795}

for every $L\ge2$, with the same $\lambda$. In raw variables each initialized
preactivation has variance at least $a^{2(\ell-1)}$, hence at least one.

#### 4. Explicit controlled primal bounds {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21800}

Let


$$
T_0=12/\lambda,\qquad S=a^{-L}T_0,\qquad F=8^L.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21804}

The source lemma in [Fragment H.2](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22029) applies on this control interval
because


$$
a=10^{10}/\lambda\ge10^8(1+12/\lambda).
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21809}

For completeness the independent primal estimates used here do not
assume source bounds or a clipped energy identity. The canonical
initialized action norms are at most 2, and it suffices to bound them
by 3. Finite initialized norms $\le3$ and first projection norms $\le2$ hold
with probability tending to one. Stop at hidden joint raw displacement
$D=1$. All current adjacent norms are then $\le4$ and bottom projection
norms $\le 3$. Using ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21739]),


$$
\|H_i^\ell\|_2\le8^\ell,\qquad\|q_i^\ell\|_2\le8^{L-\ell}\|C\|_2,\qquad\|C(v)\|_2\le3Fv,\qquad D(v)\le3\sqrt L F^2v^2.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21819}

For instance each individual hidden block speed is bounded by $F\|C\|$
when $\|c\|_1\le3$: $3\cdot2\cdot8^{L-\ell}\cdot8^{\ell-1}\le F$, with the same bound for the
bottom block. Summing squares over the L blocks and integrating C gives
an even smaller constant than in ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21819]). On a positive Euler mesh use
$\sum_jh_jv_j\le v_k^2/2$. Thus the estimates exclude a first discrete
overshoot as well as a continuous first exit. The finite zero-readout
comparison program obeys them; for the actual finite $C(0)$ its vanishing
initial norm is added until the fixed-cap bridge removes that error.

Telescoping each forward layer against its own initialized state gives


$$
\|Z_i^\ell-Z_i^\ell(0)\|_2\le4\cdot8^{\ell-1}D,\qquad\|H_i^\ell-H_i^\ell(0)\|_2\le8^\ell D.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21834}

Indeed the preactivation difference is at most
$8^{\ell-1}D+3\cdot2$ times the preceding preactivation difference; the displayed
bound is preserved by induction and holds at $\ell=1$. With $Q_L$ the
normalized top feature Gram, ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21819])-([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21834]) yield


$$
\|Q_L-Q_L(0)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le6F^2D\le18\sqrt L F^4S^2.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21842}

Let $J_{h}$ be the true hidden differential of $F=(F_1,F_2,F_3)$, and $U_{h,R}$
the clipped hidden direction map from coefficient vectors. Each
sample's hidden gradient has joint norm at most $\sqrt LF\|C\|$. Since
there are three samples, both operator norms are $\le\sqrt{3L}F\|C\|$,
and therefore


$$
\|J_hU_{h,R}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le3LF^2\|C\|^2\le27LF^4S^2.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21851}

Finally, ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21834]) and $a\ge1$ give a bound in ORIGINAL preactivation coordinates:


$$
\max_{i,\ell}\|z_i^\ell-z_i^\ell(0)\|_2\le a^{L-1}FD\le3\sqrt L(512/a)^LT_0^2/a.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21856}

All these estimates are uniform in cap and apply to every control prefix.

Here is an explicit arithmetic check with comfortable slack, uniform in
$L\ge2$. We have $0<\lambda<1$ and $a=10^{10}/\lambda$. For $0<q\le1/4$, the sequence
$Lq^L$ decreases for $L\ge2$, and $\sqrt Lq^L\le Lq^L\le2q^2$. Consequently


$$
\begin{aligned}18\sqrt L(4096/a^2)^LT_0^2&\le36(4096/a^2)^2(144/\lambda^2)<\lambda/4,\\27L(4096/a^2)^LT_0^2&\le54(4096/a^2)^2(144/\lambda^2)<\lambda/4,\\3\sqrt L(64/a^2)^LT_0^2&<1/4,\\3\sqrt L(512/a)^LT_0^2/a&\le6(512/a)^2(144/\lambda^2)/a<\sqrt{\eta_0}/2.\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21865}

For example the largest numerator in the first two lines is less than
$1.4\cdot10^{11}$, whereas $a^4\lambda^2=10^{40}/\lambda^2$. The last line is at most
$3\cdot10^8\lambda/10^{30}$. These inequalities also verify the stopped primal
ball premise with strict slack. By ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21795]), ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21842]), ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21851]),


$$
Q_L\ge3\lambda I/4,\qquad\|J_hU_{h,R}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lambda/4.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21878}

#### 5. Global fitting for clipped flows and the nonlinear source estimate {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21880}

The clipped physical raw direction is $-a^L$ times the normalized update
field with coefficients r. Differentiating the actual predictions
$f=a^LF$ along that direction gives exactly


$$
\dot r=-a^{2L}(Q_L+J_hU_{h,R})r.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21886}

The hidden contribution need not be symmetric or positive. Its absolute
operator bound in ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21878]) is enough. Before $v(t)$ reaches S,


$$
(d/dt)\|r\|^2\le-\lambda a^{2L}\|r\|^2,\qquad\|r(t)\|\le\sqrt3\exp[-\lambda a^{2L}t/2],\qquad v(t)\le a^L\sqrt3\int_0^\infty\|r(t)\|\,dt\le6/(\lambda a^L)=S/2.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21891}

Thus the controlled-budget stop cannot occur. Bounded clipped raw
speeds give a strongly Cauchy endpoint at any finite maximal physical
time; local Lipschitz existence from that endpoint continues the path.
Every clipped population flow is global. This did not assign the true
loss-energy identity to a clipped update.

The key new analytic estimate is proved in [Fragment H.2](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22029). In the
normalization ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21705]), with $F=8^L$, it constructs the ACTUAL strict forward
response densities and causal backward rows on every positive mesh,
uniformly in the incoming-field caps. Its constants obey


$$
\alpha_\ell=32^\ell\cdot3F^2,\qquad b_\ell=2048^{L-\ell+1}B_0,\quad B_0\le4FT_0/a,\qquad\alpha_\ell Sb_\ell\le24576(1048576/a)^L64^{-\ell}T_0^2/a.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21907}

Condition ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21809]) makes the last product $<10^{-10}$ and the associated
random derivative exponential parameter $<10^{-8}$ at every layer and
every finite depth. The crucial estimate retains actual Gaussian
covariances and current transpose returns: at the SAME source arrays,
the Gaussian part of $q_\ell$ has scale controlled by its already proved
raw $L^{2}$ scale plus $b_\ell/K_\ell$. The bounded forward nonlinear remainder
$\arctan(K_\ell Z)/K_\ell$ compensates the curvature $K_\ell$. Strict production
then improves each coefficient radius, rather than assuming it remains
bounded. The proof supplies full local identities and constants.

Rewriting a fine physical Euler mesh by $h_j=a^L\Delta t_j\|r_j\|_1$ and
$c_j=-r_j/\|r_j\|_1$ reproduces its normalized clipped updates. Freeze
these deterministic causal contractions in named-source derivatives.
The strict budget $S/2$ and fixed-cap Euler convergence imply $\sum h_j<S$
on sufficiently fine meshes on each physical horizon. The source
lemma therefore yields, for fixed L,a, constants $M,c>0$ independent of
physical time and cap, for all normalized incoming fields Q,


$$
\sup_{R,t}\|Q_R(t)\|_p\le M\sqrt p,\quad p\ge2,\qquad\sup_{R,t}\|Q_R(t)\mathbf1_{\{|Q_R(t)|>u\}}\|_2\le M\exp(-cu^2).
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21930}

No temporal independence and no random time-maximum bound is used.

#### 6. Global population and finite-algorithm bridges {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21935}

[Fragment H.3](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22217) states the finite-depth bridge precisely and checks
its hypotheses here. Its local source is the finite adaptive Gaussian
conditioning construction in the existing self-contained manuscript,
special-data [Section III.F](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l3785) and [Fragment A](02-gaussian-reuse.qmd#sec-docs-global-nonlinear-l1840), together with the fully derived cap/velocity/path
arguments in special-data [Section III.V](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l4992). Those arguments handle finitely many named
independent matrices by induction, and apply to the layer-dependent
bounded-derivative $\psi_\ell$ in ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21705]). The following are the substantive
verification steps, not additional assumptions.

* Finite clipped programs have bounded $C^1$ coordinate derivatives,
  deterministic causal scalar contractions, finitely many independent
  Gaussian matrices used in both orientations, and the required
  singular-query regularization. They give common $L^{2}$ layer spaces,
  bounded initialized actions and genuine adjoints. Their learned
  rank-one integrals are Hilbert--Schmidt.
* ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21819]), ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21865]), ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21891]) give global clipped reference paths, compact-time
  bounds and strict continuation slack. ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21907])-([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21930]) give the cap-independent
  tails required for removal. The one-sided gate comparison has one
  factor $R$, not $R^L$, and uses tails of the reference only. Its error is
  $C_T\exp(C_TR-cR^2)$. Hence clipped paths and their raw velocities are
  uniformly Cauchy in the raw Hilbert norm on each compact interval.
* The same comparison against any bounded-primal uncut competitor proves
  uniqueness and reached-state restart, with its own residual vector.
  No folding/exchange symmetry, positive input-Gram assumption or
  affine fitting clock is used.
* At fixed cap, coarse-mesh fixed-program width convergence and
  width-independent raw Euler stability give the finite GF/GD limits.
  The independent finite random readout has RMS $O_P(n^{-1})$, which is
  retained before this comparison. Ordered truncations for each appended
  true-backward and velocity product give the true raw kernels and
  velocity laws. State/velocity compactness and integrated speed bounds
  give the path laws. All iteration counts are finite once L and the
  observation horizon are fixed.

Taking the strong cap limit in ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21891]) proves ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21661]). The limiting vector
field is the actual raw gradient by the scalar predictor differential
and genuine adjunction, so its exact energy identity also holds.
[Fragment H.3](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22217) spells out the estimates, observation definitions
and the order of limits; no different training scheme is substituted.

#### 7. Absolute nonaffinity and initial motion {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21977}

For a square-integrable real X, write


$$
R(X)=\inf_{\alpha,\beta}\mathbb E[(\operatorname{atan}X-\alpha-\beta X)^2].
$$

Every optimal regression slope can be chosen in $[0,1]$. When $\operatorname{Var}(X)>0$,
this follows from the independent-copy identity for covariance and
$0\le(\arctan x-\arctan y)/(x-y)\le1$; when $\operatorname{Var}(X)=0$ choose slope zero. If b is
such a slope at Y, the function atan x-bx is 1-Lipschitz, and testing
Y's optimal affine predictor at X shows


$$
\sqrt{R(X)}\le\sqrt{R(Y)}+\|X-Y\|_2.
$$

Interchanging X and Y proves that $\sqrt R$ is 1-Lipschitz under $L^2$
coupling. By the cubic test ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21765])-([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21771]), $R(\sigma G)\ge\eta_0$ for every $\sigma\ge1$.
Combine the initialized variances after ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21795]) with ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21856])-([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21865]) to get
$R(z_i^\ell(t))\ge\eta_0/4$, first for every clipped path and then for its
strong limit. Absorbing the linear $a*z$ into the free affine predictor
gives ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21675]).

[Fragment H.4](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22531) proves ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21684]) and all individual initial-motion claims
by induction on initialized Gaussian queries. Positive top feature
Gram and the nonconstant positive activation derivative give a positive
definite top backward Gram. Actual transpose returns preserve a fresh
positive Gaussian covariance at every lower layer. Each new forward
acceleration query has a Gaussian innovation orthogonal to the original
forward features, of strictly positive variance; it cannot cancel with
the current backward return. This supplies every sample's motion for
generic triples without permutation symmetry.

#### 8. Scope and comparison with the convex mixture {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22008}

Excluding $\rho=-1$ removes the direct antipodal oddness obstruction.
It does not imply positive input-Gram eigenvalues for three inputs:
three planar unit vectors at angles 120 degrees still sum to zero.
Nevertheless ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21760])-([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21784]) show that their nonlinear initialized features
are independent. There is no counterexample here to the positive odd
convex mixture.

The new theorem uses a second device: a large overall gain. In ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21643]),
$\phi_\delta=2a_\delta[(1/2)z+(1/2)\arctan z]$. Dividing by $2a_\delta$ changes
the hidden features at every layer and changes their raw gradient
dynamics. Thus the theorem neither establishes an energy-normalized
activation nor proves a threshold for the exact unit-sum mixture.

The power $\delta^{-2}$ in the sufficient gain is derived explicitly, uniformly
over all fixed finite depths. No matching necessary gain lower bound is
proved; the initialized cubic separation scale $\delta^2$ is a different
claim whose sharpness does not establish gain optimality. A numerical
prefactor of approximately $2.77\cdot10^{13}$ in ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21643]) is deliberately conservative.

### H.2. Direct large-gain source response {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22029}

Within this proof unit, unqualified section and equation numbers are local.

#### 1. Exact normalization and statement {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22033}

Fix finite hidden depth $L\ge2$ and three RMS-unit inputs. Put $\rho=a^{-L}$, $K_l=a^{l-1}$,


$$
X_l=H_l/a^l,\qquad Y_l=Z_l/a^{l-1},\qquad\psi_l(y)=y+K_l^{-1}\operatorname{atan}(K_ly).
$$

The raw hidden parameters are unchanged. Initially set the linear time coordinate $u=a^Lt$ and retain the ORIGINAL raw readout C. Write s for a general controlled clock; choosing $s=u$ gives the physical residual controls below. The exact controlled equations are


$$
C'=\sum_ic_iX_{L,i},\qquad V_l'=\sum_ic_id_{l,i}\otimes X_{l-1,i},\quad2\le l\le L,\qquad w'=\sum_ic_id_{1,i}u_i,\qquad d_l=\psi_l'(Y_l)q_l,\qquad q_L=C,\quad q_l=A_{l+1}^*d_{l+1},\qquad Y_l=A_lX_{l-1},\quad X_l=\psi_l(Y_l),\quad Y_1=\langle w,u\rangle.
$$

Actual outputs are $f_i=a^L\langle C,X_{L,i}\rangle$. Original GF has $c_i=y_i-f_i$. The lemma allows ANY deterministic bounded controls $\|c(s)\|_1\le3$.

::: {#lem-docs-special-data-limits-l22051}
The case $T=0$ is trivial. Let $T>0$, $S=a^{-L}T$, and $a\ge10^8(1+T)$. Then on $[0,S]$, incoming-field-capped source constructions and their finite Euler programs have strict raw hidden-ball slack, cap/mesh-uniform marginal subGaussian fields, integrable source derivatives, and the explicit actual coefficient box below. The gain condition is independent of $L$; each width limit still fixes finite L and a first. The displayed source construction has the population initialization $C(0)=0$. The finite Gaussian readout is retained when applying the width bridge.

The existing finite-depth population bridge therefore gives the strong uncut controlled population flow on this interval. A global original-GF application separately needs an accumulated residual-clock bound. This lemma alone does not assert fitting.

:::

#### 2. Primal slack without capped energy {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22055}

Assume initialized adjacent action norms $\le3$ and first-layer input projection norms $\le2$ (these bounds also hold with probability tending to one in the finite Gaussian model). Stop when the joint raw norm of HIDDEN parameter increments reaches one. Then current action norms $\le4$ and $\|Y_1\|_2\le3$. Since $|\psi_l(y)|\le2|y|$, all forward norms are $\le F=8^L$.

For smooth clips $|\tau_R(q)|\le|q|$, $|\tau_R'|\le1$ use


$$
D_{l,R}(z,q)=q+g(K_lz)\tau_R(q),\qquad g(v)=(1+v^2)^{-1}.
$$

Thus $|D|\le2|q|$. A common normalized incoming cap Rcap corresponds to raw layer-dependent caps $a^{L-l}R_{\mathrm{cap}}$, because the original raw incoming field at layer l is $a^{L-l}q_l$. These caps are an approximation scheme for the unchanged raw GF, not a change of metric. Readout integration gives, without energy,


$$
\|C(s)\|_2\le3Fs\le R,\quad R=3FS,\qquad\|q_{l,i}\|_2\le Q_l=8^{L-l}R,\qquad\|d_{l,i}\|_2\le2Q_l.
$$

Each hidden update block has norm $\le FR$. The joint hidden displacement is therefore $\le$


$$
3\sqrt L F^2S^2=3\sqrt L(64/a^2)^LT^2<1/4.
$$

This excludes first exit, also at arbitrary finite Euler nodes by summing their step lengths. Under the gain condition, $\max_lQ_l\le1/2$, so $\max_l\|d_l\|_2\le1$. Actual preactivation $L^{2}$ norms are $\le F$ independently of source coefficient bounds.

#### 3. Exact local source system {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22075}

Freeze deterministic source arrays, controls and source covariances. At layer l write


$$
Y_l=\xi_l+\mathcal A_ld_l,\qquad q_l=\zeta_l+\mathcal B_{l+1}X_l,\qquad X_l=\psi_l(Y_l),\qquad d_l=D_{l,R}(Y_l,q_l).
$$

$\mathcal{A}_l$ is strict and $\mathcal{B}_{l+1}$ causal. At the bottom $\xi_1$ is the repeated Gaussian root and $\mathcal{A}_1$ has blocks $h_j\Gamma\operatorname{diag}(c_j)$, strict density $\le3$. At the top $\zeta_L=0$ and $\mathcal{B}_{L+1}$ is the readout integrator with causal row $\le3S$. Remaining primitive groups are the original jointly centered Gaussian groups, with full second-moment covariances and the named-slot convention if singular.

For an internal initialized matrix the exact coefficients are


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathcal A_{l+1,kj})_{uv}&=\mathbb E\partial_{\zeta_{l,j,v}}X_{l,k,u}+h_jc_{j,v}\mathbb E[X_{l,k,u}X_{l,j,v}],\quad j<k,\\(\mathcal B_{l,kj})_{uv}&=\mathbb E\partial_{\xi_{l,j,v}}d_{l,k,u}+\mathbf1_{\{j<k\}}h_jc_{j,v}\mathbb E[d_{l,k,u}d_{l,j,v}],\quad j\le k.\end{aligned}
$$

All current returns are included. Within each time row the order is $\mathcal{A}_2,\ldots,\mathcal{A}_L,\mathcal{B}_L,\ldots,\mathcal{B}_2$.

Use the induced infinity norm on three-sample blocks and full row sums. Locally assume strict density $\alpha$ for $\mathcal A_l$ and causal row b for $\mathcal B_{l+1}$. Let $r=\alpha Sb$.

#### 4. Same-array Gaussian-part identity {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22099}

Write


$$
r_l=K_l^{-1}\operatorname{atan}(K_lY_l),\quad|r_l|\le\pi/(2K_l),\qquad e_l=g(K_lY_l)\tau_R(q_l),\quad|e_l|\le|q_l|.
$$

Thus $X_l=Y_l+r_l$ and $d_l=q_l+e_l$. At the SAME actual coefficient arrays put


$$
R_{\mathrm{loc}}=(I-\mathcal A_l\mathcal B_{l+1})^{-1},\qquad U=R_{\mathrm{loc}}\mathcal A_l,\qquad L_{\mathrm{loc}}=(I-\mathcal B_{l+1}\mathcal A_l)^{-1},\qquad Y_G=R_{\mathrm{loc}}\xi_l+U\zeta_l,\qquad q_G=L_{\mathrm{loc}}\zeta_l+\mathcal B_{l+1}R_{\mathrm{loc}}\xi_l.
$$

These are centered Gaussian combinations of frozen-source groups. Exact elimination gives


$$
Y_l-Y_G=Ue_l+U\mathcal B_{l+1}r_l,\qquad q_l-q_G=\mathcal B_{l+1}Ue_l+L_{\mathrm{loc}}\mathcal B_{l+1}r_l.
$$

For $r\le1/8$ the two resolvent rows are $\le2$, $|U|_{\mathrm{row}}\le2\alpha S$, and $|\mathcal{B}U|_{\mathrm{row}}\le2r$. Consequently


$$
\|q_l-q_G\|_p\le2r\|q_l\|_p+\pi b/K_l.
$$

The independently proved actual $L^{2}$ bound implies


$$
\|q_G\|_2\le2Q_l+4b/K_l.
$$

Gaussian moments and absorption give, for $p\ge2$,


$$
\max_i\|q_{l,i}\|_p\le20(Q_l+b/K_l)\sqrt p,\qquad\|K_l\max_i|q_{l,i}|\|_p\le W_l\sqrt p,\qquad W_l=60(n_l+b),\quad n_l=K_lQ_l.
$$

The bounded nonlinear remainder $\pi/(2K_l)$ compensates the local curvature $K_l$. No independence between Gaussian and remainder is needed.

Likewise,


$$
\max_i\|Y_{l,i}\|_p\le[F+50\alpha S(Q_l+b/K_l)]\sqrt p.
$$

In the actual box below the bracket is $\le2F$, so $\|X_{l,i}\|_p\le4F\sqrt p$. These are suprema of marginal norms, not random time maxima.

#### 5. Exact source derivatives and coefficient production {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22142}

With $G=\operatorname{diag}\psi_l'(Y)$, $V=\operatorname{diag}\partial_qD$, $N=\operatorname{diag}\partial_zD$,


$$
\|G\|,\|V\|\le2,\qquad\|N_k\|\le K_l\max_i|q_{l,k,i}|.
$$

Any named source Jacobian J of Y obeys exactly


$$
J=I_\xi+\mathcal A_l[NJ+V(I_\zeta+\mathcal B_{l+1}GJ)].
$$

Current $\mathcal{B}_{l+1,kk}$ is retained. Strict $\mathcal{A}_l$ prevents a current algebraic loop. Finite Volterra iteration gives


$$
\begin{aligned}\|\partial_\xi Y_{l,k}\|_{\mathrm{row}}&\le E_k,&\|\partial_{\zeta_j}Y_{l,k}\|&\le2\alpha h_jE_k,\quad j<k,\\E_k&=\exp\!\left(4\alpha bS+\alpha\sum_{r<k}h_rK_l\max_i|q_{l,r,i}|\right),\\\|\partial_\xi d_{l,k}\|_{\mathrm{row}}&\le(K_l\max_i|q_{l,k,i}|+4b)E_k.\end{aligned}
$$

The subGaussian criterion and weighted Jensen (no temporal independence) give


$$
\mathbb E\exp(u|Z|)\le2\exp(2\exp(1)M^2u^2)
$$

when $\|Z\|_p\le M\sqrt p$. If $\alpha Sb\le10^{-9}$ and $\alpha SW_l\le10^{-6}$, safe production bounds are


$$
\alpha_{l+1,\mathrm{new}}\le3F^2+16\alpha,\qquad b_{l-1,\mathrm{new}}\le512(n_l+b)+3S.
$$

For the reverse response, Cauchy--Schwarz bounds its expectation by


$$
\sqrt2(\sqrt2W_l+4b)\exp(4\alpha bS+4\exp(1)\alpha^2S^2W_l^2)<512(n_l+b).
$$

The reverse learned contraction is $\le3S$ since $\|d_l\|_2\le1$; the forward learned density is $\le3F^2$.

#### 6. Explicit box uniform over finite depths {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22180}

For $a\ge8$,


$$
n_l=3F(T/a)(8/a)^{L-l},\qquad n_{\max}=3FT/a.
$$

Set


$$
B_0=n_{\max}+3S\le4FT/a,\qquad\alpha_l=32^l\cdot3F^2,\qquad b_l=2048^{L-l+1}B_0,\quad1\le l\le L.
$$

Here $b_{l}$ bounds incoming $\mathcal{B}_{l+1}$. Actual top row $3S$ is strictly inside $b_L$ and bottom density $3$ is strictly inside $\alpha_1$.

Keeping every depth factor,


$$
\alpha_lS\le3(2048/a)^LT,\qquad\alpha_lSb_l\le24576(1048576/a)^L64^{-l}T^2/a\le384(1048576/a)^LT^2/a.
$$

For $a\ge10^8(1+T)$, $L\ge2$,


$$
\alpha_lS<10^{-8},\qquad\alpha_lSb_l<10^{-10},\qquad\alpha_lSW_l<10^{-8}.
$$

Indeed $n_l\le B_0\le b_l/2048$, so $W_l\le61b_l$. All preceding estimates apply and strictly improve the box:


$$
\alpha_{l+1,\mathrm{new}}\le3F^2+16\alpha_l\le17\alpha_l<32\alpha_l=\alpha_{l+1},\qquad b_{l-1,\mathrm{new}}\le512(n_l+b_l)+3S<514b_l<2048b_l=b_{l-1}.
$$

Chronological induction proves the ACTUAL box on every finite mesh. A forward row uses previously constructed reverse history; a reverse row is built after the current higher reverse row. There is no circular radius premise and no smallest-step denominator.

### H.3. Canonical construction, cap removal and complete observation limits {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22217}

Within this proof unit, unqualified section and equation numbers are local.

#### 1. Finite programs and common action spaces {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22221}

A program has a fixed finite number of instructions on layer-typed
vectors: independent Gaussian roots; fixed $C^1$ coordinate maps with
bounded continuous first derivatives; linear combinations; applications
of any of the $L-1$ initialized independent Gaussian adjacent matrices or
their transposes; and causal scalar feedback from same-layer inner
products through locally Lipschitz scalar maps. Each fixed program's
within-layer joint empirical laws, including second moments, converge
in probability in $W_{2}$ along the full width sequence. An oriented matrix
call on input h is represented by its centered Gaussian source plus the
sum of its expected named derivatives against earlier opposite-orientation
sources, multiplied by those opposite inputs. Each oriented source
group's covariance is the FULL Gram of its actual inputs. Different
oriented groups are independent. Named slots remain separate even when
source covariances are singular; all scalar feedback, expectations and
covariances are frozen in those derivatives.

Here is why the existing proof applies to $L-1$ matrices. Conditional on
previous queries of a particular Gaussian matrix, its unused block is
$P_{\mathrm{left}}GP_{\mathrm{right}}$; all other matrices remain separately conditioned
through their own transcripts. The next query is the conditional mean
plus this independent Gaussian innovation. Empirical bounded-test and
second-moment concentration identify its next scalar law. Query-input
perturbation by independent Gaussian noise makes each provisional Gram
invertible. Fixed-program bounded-operator stability removes that noise;
positive-semidefinite square-root continuity couples the limiting
covariances at singularities. Induction counts instructions, not layers.
Adding finitely many matrices only adds finitely many such steps. No
source-covariance inverse remains in the final identity.

A countable language including all rational linear combinations,
bounded smooth coordinate probes, integer clips, rational meshes and
both action orientations generates one probability space per layer.
Finite-program consistency supplies their joint cylinder laws. On the
dense span of generated fields, the finite norm and inner-product
identities pass to the limit. Hence each initialized action extends
boundedly to its layer $L^{2}$ space, and its reverse is its genuine Hilbert
adjoint. Approximation by bounded smooth cylinder functions gives density
in $L^{2}$. These are the canonical initialization spaces, not arbitrary
bounded operators with the same norms.

The population parameter space is the first-layer vector $L^{2}$ space,
the affine spaces $A_{\ell,0}+\operatorname{HS}(H_{\ell-1},H_\ell)$, and the top readout $H_L$.
The raw metric is the one in [Fragment H.1](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21616). Rank-one velocities have norm
$\|u\otimes v\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=\|u\|_2\|v\|_2$, so continuous raw updates integrate in
HS. Their reversed increments are their actual adjoints.

In our application, every $\psi_\ell$ has bounded continuous derivative and
every fixed clipped backward gate $D_{\ell,R}$ has bounded continuous first
derivatives. Scalar physical feedback is the residual vector, a locally
Lipschitz function of inner products on bounded primal balls. All the
finite-program hypotheses have therefore been checked. The effective
residual-clock controls are frozen only in formal source derivatives;
the physical residual feedback remains part of the actual dynamics.

#### 2. Fixed-cap existence and asymmetric comparison {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22277}

For fixed finite L,a,R, forward and backward induction on a bounded
primal ball gives a raw locally Lipschitz field. The first projection
map is bounded in the raw metric; every next layer uses a bounded
action, a Lipschitz activation and continuous bilinear evaluation.
The clipped gates are globally Lipschitz. Each rank-one update is
locally Lipschitz by


$$
\|u\otimes v-u'\otimes v'\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\|u-u'\|_2\|v\|_2+\|u'\|_2\|v-v'\|_2.
$$

The integral map is a contraction on a sufficiently short interval.
Strong Cauchy endpoints and the uniform primal bounds extend the clipped
solution. [Fragment H.1](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21616) Sections [4](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21800)--[5](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21880) establish its global continuation with
strict residual-clock slack, independently of all cap-removal arguments.

For $R'\ge R$, including $R'=\infty$, the normalized gates obey


$$
|D_{\ell,R'}(z,q)-D_{\ell,R}(z',q')|\le2|q-q'|+2K_\ell R|z-z'|+2|q'|\mathbf1_{\{|q'|>R\}}.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22296}

To verify ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22296]), first change q to $q'$ in $D_{\ell,R'}$, which costs at most
$2|q-q'|$. In the remaining nonlinear term use the decomposition


$$
[g(K_\ell z)-g(K_\ell z')]\tau_R(q')+g(K_\ell z)[\tau_{R'}(q')-\tau_R(q')],
$$

where $\tau_{R'}$ in this display denotes the clip at level $R'$, not a
derivative. Bounded $g'$, $|\tau_R|\le2R$, and equality of both clips inside
[-R,R] give the other two terms. This asymmetric decomposition requires
tail control only of the reference state $(z',q')$.

Forward state differences are bounded by C times the raw state
difference. Backward substitution through any finite L multiplies an
existing discrepancy only by a bounded action and the gate's q-Lipschitz
constant 2. Every newly introduced factor R multiplies a FORWARD
discrepancy already bounded separately. It does not multiply a previous
R term. Rank-one updates and residual feedback then give


$$
\|F_{R'}(\Theta)-F_R(\Theta')\|_{\mathrm{raw}}\le C_{L,a,b}(1+R)\|\Theta-\Theta'\|_{\mathrm{raw}}+C_{L,a,b}\sum_Q\|Q(\Theta')\mathbf1_{\{|Q(\Theta')|>R\}}\|_2.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22318}

Here $F_{R'}$ means the field at cap R', b denotes the common primal ball,
and the finite sum runs over the reference's incoming fields. The same
bound holds for all backward field differences. Physical gain factors
are fixed constants $a^L$. Coefficient differences in residual feedback
are bounded by the already controlled forward and readout differences.

[Fragment H.2](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22029) and [Fragment H.1](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21616) ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l21930]) provide Gaussian reference tails
uniformly in time and cap. Integrating ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22318]) and Gronwall's inequality
therefore gives on each physical $[0,T]$


$$
\sup_{t\le T}\|\Theta_{R'}(t)-\Theta_R(t)\|_{\mathrm{raw}}+\sup_{t\le T}\|F_{R'}(\Theta_{R'}(t))-F_R(\Theta_R(t))\|_{\mathrm{raw}}\le C_T\exp(C_TR-cR^2).
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22332}

Polynomial factors in R are absorbed into $C_T\exp(C_TR)$. Thus paths
and raw velocities are uniformly Cauchy. Their limit is strong $C^1$ and
satisfies the uncut equations by ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22318]) and bounded-multiplier continuity.
Taking integer caps and horizons gives one consistent global solution.

For any other strong uncut solution with bounded primal quantities on
$[0,T]$, compare it to the same clipped reference using ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22318]). Only its
primal bound enters $C_T$; its own tails are not assumed. Equation $(27)$
forces equality in the limit. At a reached time t0, the initial error
against the clipped reference is already of the form ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22332]), and another
factor $\exp(C_TR)$ still tends to zero. This proves uniqueness of
continuation from that state. No arbitrary-state $L^{2}$ local theorem for
the uncut vector field is used.

#### 3. Strong chain rule and raw gradient identification {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22350}

If $X(t)$ is a strong $C^1$ $L^2$ curve and $\psi$ is $C^{1}$ with bounded continuous
derivative, then $\psi(X(t))$ is strong $C^{1}$ and has derivative $\psi'(X)X'$.
Indeed integrate X' to obtain almost-everywhere absolutely continuous
coordinate versions and apply the scalar chain rule. The multiplier
product is $L^{2}$-continuous: if $X_k\to X$ and $P_k\to P$ in $L^2$, split


$$
\psi'(X_k)P_k-\psi'(X)P=\psi'(X_k)(P_k-P)+[\psi'(X_k)-\psi'(X)]P.
$$

Boundedness treats the first term; convergence in probability and an
integrable |P|² dominator treat the second. The coordinate integral
identity passes to $L^{2}$. Repeating with the continuous bilinear action
product rule proves the strong forward chain rule at all L layers.

The scalar predictor's hidden directional derivative pairs each raw
increment against the corresponding backward rank-one field. This
follows by repeated Hilbert adjunction and Cauchy--Schwarz; all gates
are bounded and all fields are $L^2$. The first-block factor is $1/d$ in
the original w coordinates. The scalar derivative is continuous in
the raw state: the same bounded-multiplier argument treats varying
backward fields. Consequently the limiting autonomous equations are
the raw Hilbert gradient flow of the stated squared loss, and its
energy identity follows by the scalar chain rule. No Frechet
differentiability of the activation map on a whole $L^{2}$ ball is asserted.

#### 4. Fixed-cap finite GF and raw GD {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22377}

At a fixed cap and physical horizon, take a coarse mesh of finitely
many time steps. The finite-program theorem identifies its full-width
limit. Scalar feedback uses all three residuals, not a prescribed
population residual in place of the actual finite residual. A sufficiently
large finite primal ball contains these coarse nodes with high
probability: first-layer and readout norms converge, and each hidden
matrix increment is bounded by the sum of its rank-one update lengths,
whose finitely many contractions converge.

On that enlarged ball the clipped field has norm M0 and Lipschitz
constant L0 independent of width. The exact GF/Euler local defect for
a step h is $\le L_0M_0h^2/2$. Iteration gives a uniform state error bounded
by $C_T$ times the mesh size, with first-exit slack keeping all states
in that ball. This proves finite GF versus the coarse Euler program,
and simultaneous raw Euler with fine step $n^{-2}$ versus that GF. It
does not apply fixed-program convergence to $n^2$ growing instructions.
Take width first at the coarse mesh, then send that fixed mesh size
to zero. The population coarse Euler program converges by the same
Hilbert-space estimate. Its limit is the unique clipped solution.

The actual finite Gaussian $C_{n}(0)$ has $\mathbb{E}(\|C_n(0)\|_{\mathrm{Euclidean}}^2/n)=n^{-2}$. Its initial
discrepancy from the zero-readout finite comparator is $O_P(n^{-1})$.
The fixed-cap Lipschitz comparison bounds the propagated discrepancy
by $\exp(L_0T)O_P(n^{-1})$. Thus zero is the population initial readout;
neither actual finite GF nor actual finite GD is initialized at zero
by substitution.

For the uncut finite algorithms, apply ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22318]) with the finite clipped
reference. At fixed cap, the finite empirical incoming tails converge
to their population reference tails, using continuous truncations and
second-moment convergence. Uniformity in time comes from a finite time
net and the fixed-cap strong moduli described below. Finite first-exit
comparison then gives limsup-width errors of the form ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22332]). For GD,
the discrete version has the same single factor R and a vanishing
fixed-cap $O(n^{-2})$ consistency term; the hidden fields are recomputed
from the raw linear interpolation. Send width to infinity first and
then R to infinity. This gives both algorithms the same full-sequence
limit. A subsequence argument upgrades any almost-sure extracted
comparisons to convergence in probability of the original full sequence.

#### 5. True kernels, velocities and paths {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22419}

For the original raw model let $b_i^\ell$ be the TRUE backward fields.
The $L+1$ kernel blocks are


$$
K^1_{ij}=\Gamma_{ij}\langle b_i^1,b_j^1\rangle,\qquad K^\ell_{ij}=\langle b_i^\ell,b_j^\ell\rangle\langle h_i^{(\ell-1)},h_j^{(\ell-1)}\rangle,\quad2\le\ell\le L,\qquad K^{(L+1)}_{ij}=\langle h_i^L,h_j^L\rangle.
$$

Every inner product is within its designated layer. These are the true
raw kernels even when observed at an auxiliary clipped state; clipped
update fields are not substituted for their b fields.

The fixed-cap observation proof in special-data [Section III.V](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l4992) [V.3](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l5115)--[V.6](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l5224) has these
premises: bounded clipped primal states on the observation interval;
bounded continuous coordinate derivatives; deterministic causal
source coefficients; finite-dimensional Gaussian query perturbations
continuous under vanishing perturbation; and the already proved
fixed-mesh primary width laws. All were verified in Sections [1](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22221)--[4](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22377).
Its depth induction proceeds as follows.

A fresh independent Gaussian probe added to any named answer slot
changes the recomputed clipped raw trajectory by $C\epsilon$, or by
$Ch_j\varepsilon$ if inserted only at a strictly past time j. Gaussian
integration by parts with deterministic coefficients frozen bounds
the ABSOLUTE ROW OF EXPECTED source derivatives, after choosing signs,
by C or $Ch_j$. Current reverse responses are retained and constructed
in descending layer order. With these deterministic rows bounded,
differentiate the local source equations pointwise. Bounded gate
derivatives and the strict forward time order yield a discrete
Volterra inequality $U_k\le C+C\sum_{j<k}h_jU_j$ for the maximum primary
absolute derivative row. Summation of nested time integrals costs at
most the fixed horizon. The $L-1$ backward levels are a finite causal
substitution, so $U_k\le C\exp(CT)$. Repeating with Lp norms gives primary
source bounds $C\sqrt p$. No matrix $L^p\text{-to-}L^p$ action bound is assumed.

Append instantaneous velocity queries in ascending layer order. With
$P_i^\ell=\dot z_i^\ell$ and $U_i^\ell=\phi'(z_i^\ell)P_i^\ell$,


$$
P_i^1=\dot w\cdot x_i,\qquad P_i^\ell=\dot A_\ell h_i^{(\ell-1)}+A_\ell U_i^{(\ell-1)}.
$$

The learned action part is an explicit rank integral. For each newly
appended initialized-action call, its reverse-source derivative is a
sum of the previously bounded derivatives and a bounded gate derivative
times the incoming velocity. Its Gaussian source variance is the actual
$L^{2}$ norm of that incoming query. The preceding layer and primal raw
direction bounds control this norm before any higher-layer velocity
estimate is invoked. Induction yields fixed-cap marginal $C_{L,R,T}$
$\sqrt p$ bounds for appended velocities on population fine meshes and
flows. Same-family joint time and sample covariances are retained.

Products $\phi'(Z)P$ do not have globally bounded derivatives in $(Z,P)$.
The observation proof therefore uses $\phi'(Z)\tau_M(P)$, a legitimate
bounded-derivative instruction, and removes the clips in the following
order: keep the new outer query cap M fixed while removing all earlier
inner velocity caps, then remove M using the proved marginal tail
bounds. True-backward observations use the same descending ordered
truncation. This verifies the fixed-program laws of the unbounded
products rather than assuming them. The construction uses L steps,
each already supplied with the previous step's norm and tail estimate.

For a state/direction pair and a reference pair, the deterministic
product comparison has the form


$$
\|\phi'(Z)P-\phi'(Z_0)P_0\|_2\le C\|P-P_0\|_2+CM\|Z-Z_0\|_2+C\|P_0\mathbf1_{\{|P_0|>M\}}\|_2.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22485}

It follows by splitting P0 at M and using bounded $\phi'$ and $\phi''$.
Forward induction leaves one M times the primary state discrepancy,
plus the reference velocity tails. At fixed cap, the proved moment
bounds and raw Lipschitz state/direction estimates yield a uniform
$L^{2}$ time modulus for velocities (a square-root modulus suffices).
This justifies passage from finite time nets to uniform-in-time
state/velocity empirical $W_{2}$ laws. In the cap-removal step, the uncut
reference's velocity image is compact in $L^{2}$ by the strong chain rule,
which implies uniform $L^{2}$ tail removal. Equation ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22485]), with state/raw
direction convergence first and M then sent to infinity, transfers
these velocity laws to the uncut flow. It does not require an unproved
cap-uniform pointwise bound on the entire velocity path.

All true kernel terms are continuous functions of the corresponding
convergent $L^{2}$ backward and feature pairs, so their convergence is
uniform on the physical horizon. Joint observations at any fixed finite
collection of times are included by appending that finite list before
the fixed-program limit. The same applies to fixed finite generated
probes formed from layer-typed bounded-derivative maps, contractions
and either action orientation. Second moments and integrals of squared
speeds follow from the uniform $W_{2}$ state/velocity convergence.

Finally, a continuous coordinate path X with square-integrable speed
and its piecewise-linear interpolation on a mesh of size h obey


$$
\|X-\operatorname{Interp}_hX\|_\infty^2\le4h\int_0^{\top}|X'(t)|^2dt.
$$

This is the intervalwise Cauchy--Schwarz estimate and the triangle
inequality between endpoints. Apply it inside each empirical layer
law and inside the population law. Fixed-mesh joint laws converge;
the integrated speed bounds make both interpolation errors uniformly
small as h decreases. This proves $W_{2}$ convergence in the uniform path
norm, without replacing a supremum of marginal moments by a moment of
a random time supremum.

Every estimate above is for fixed finite L,a and a fixed physical
horizon. Width precedes the auxiliary cap and observation-truncation
limits. The common activation in [Fragment H.1](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l21616) is independent of L, but
the bridge constants and the width needed for a prescribed accuracy
need not be uniform in L. This distinction completes the theorem's
stated quantifiers.

### H.4. Every sample and layer moves initially at arbitrary fixed depth {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22531}

Within this proof unit, unqualified section and equation numbers are local.

#### 1. Setup and statement {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22535}

Fix an integer $L\ge2$ and three normalized inputs $u_i=x_i/\sqrt d$, with


$$
\|u_i\|=1,\qquad\Gamma_{ij}=\langle u_i,u_j\rangle,\qquad|\Gamma_{ij}|\le1-\delta\ (i\ne j),\qquad\delta>0.
$$

Only feasible data are quantified over. Let $y_{i}$ in $\{-1,1\}$, $p_i=y_i/3$, and take the same activation in every hidden layer,


$$
\phi(z)=a(z+\operatorname{atan}z),\qquad a>0.
$$

The argument in fact works for $\phi(z)=az+e\arctan z$ with any independent $a,e>0$. In the stated odd-gain case $e=a$. Write $A_l:H_{l-1}\to H_l$ for the canonical initialized action of $W^{l}$, $l=2,\ldots,L$, including its genuine adjoint. The first initialized projection tuple $Z^1$ has law $N(0,\Gamma)$, and recursively


$$
h_i^l=\phi(Z_i^l),\qquad Z_i^l=A_lh_i^{(l-1)}\ (l\ge2),\qquad D_i^l=\phi'(Z_i^l),\qquad Q_l=(\langle h_i^l,h_j^l\rangle)_{ij}.
$$

All objects in this proof unit are at initialization unless a time argument is displayed. Set


$$
H=\sum_ip_ih_i^L,\qquad\beta_i^L=D_i^LH,\qquad q_i^l=A_{l+1}^*\beta_i^{l+1},\qquad\beta_i^l=D_i^lq_i^l\ (l<L),\qquad S_l=(\langle\beta_i^l,\beta_j^l\rangle)_{ij}.
$$

The raw hidden directions are


$$
V^1=d^{-1}\sum_ip_i\beta_i^1x_i,\qquad V^l=\sum_ip_i\beta_i^l\otimes h_i^{(l-1)},\quad2\le l\le L.
$$

Their sample preactivation/feature directions are


$$
U_j^1=V^1\cdot x_j=\sum_i\Gamma_{ji}p_i\beta_i^1,\qquad t_j^l=D_j^lU_j^l,\qquad U_j^l=V^lh_j^{(l-1)}+A_lt_j^{(l-1)},\quad2\le l\le L.
$$

Every $V^l$, every $U_j^l$, and every $t_j^l$ is nonzero in its appropriate raw, HS, or $L^2$ norm. No sample permutation symmetry or scalar residual clock is assumed.

For any canonical strong physical gradient flow from $C(0)=0$ with the strong chain rule, these yield


$$
(\theta_h^l)''(0)=9V^l,\qquad(z_j^l)''(0)=9U_j^l,\qquad(h_j^l)''(0)=9t_j^l,
$$

as strong right derivatives. If $K_{\mathrm{total}}$ is the actual sum of all $L$ hidden kernel blocks and the readout block, then


$$
p^{\top}K_{\mathrm{total}}(t)p=p^{\top}K_{\mathrm{total}}(0)p+18t^2\|V\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}^2+o(t^2),
$$

where $\|V\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}^2=d\|V^1\|_2^2+\sum_{l=2}^L\|V^l\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2>0$.

#### 2. Initial forward Grams are positive, including singular $\Gamma$ {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22581}

Let G be standard normal, $H_3(z)=z^3-3z$, and


$$
b_3=\mathbb E[\operatorname{atan}(G)H_3(G)]/\sqrt6=(1-2\mathbb E[(1+G^2)^{-1}])/\sqrt6\ne0.
$$

The equality follows by Gaussian integration by parts. Strict Jensen gives $\mathbb{E}[(1+G^2)^{-1}]>1/2$, hence $b_3\ne0$.

The cubic tensor lift of three absolutely separated lines satisfies


$$
\Gamma^{\circ3}\ge[\delta^2(2-\delta)^2/3]I_3.
$$

A direct verification uses, for each i and the other indices j,k,


$$
v_{ij}=(u_i-\Gamma_{ij}u_j)/\sqrt{1-\Gamma_{ij}^2},\qquad R_i=u_i\otimes v_{ij}\otimes v_{ik}.
$$

Then $\|R_i\|=1$, $\langle u_l^{\otimes3},R_i\rangle=0$ for $l\ne i$, and the i-th pairing is at least $\delta(2-\delta)$. Applying Cauchy--Schwarz to $\sum_lc_lu_l^{\otimes3}$ and summing the resulting three inequalities proves the bound. This never inverts $\Gamma$.

Projecting the first features onto cubic Gaussian chaos gives, for $\phi=az+e\arctan z$,


$$
Q_1\ge e^2b_3^2\Gamma^{\circ3}>0.
$$

At every following layer the three centered Gaussian preactivations have a common positive marginal variance. The coefficient of the orthogonal projection of $\phi(Z_i)$ onto the Gaussian first chaos is at least $a$, because $z\arctan z\ge0$. The orthogonal residual contributes a positive semidefinite Gram. Therefore


$$
Q_l\ge a^2Q_{l-1}>0,\qquad2\le l\le L.
$$

In particular $Z^l$ has full three-dimensional Gaussian support for every $l\ge2$ and $H\ne0$. For $e=a$,


$$
\|H\|_2^2\ge a^{2L}b_3^2\delta^2(2-\delta)^2/9.
$$

Neither singularity of the first Gaussian tuple nor cancellation of an affine label direction invalidates this positivity.

#### 3. Backward Grams, all parameter blocks, and bottom sample motion {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22615}

Because $L\ge2$, $Z^L$ has a positive Gaussian density on $\mathbb{R}^3$. If $v^{\top}S_Lv=0$, continuity implies the identity


$$
\left[\sum_ip_i\phi(z_i)\right]\left[\sum_iv_i\phi'(z_i)\right]=0\ \text{on }\mathbb R^3.
$$

The first factor has no open zero set: its derivative in each coordinate is $p_i\phi'(z_i)$, which never vanishes. Consequently the second factor vanishes everywhere. Differentiating in coordinate i gives $v_i\phi''(z_i)=0$ for every $z_{i}$. Since $e>0$ and $\phi''$ is not identically zero, $v_i=0$. Thus $S_L$ is positive definite.

The exact reused-transpose initialization rule, with its returns retained, is


$$
q_i^l=\zeta_i^l+\sum_kR_{ik}^lh_k^l,\qquad1\le l<L.
$$

The coefficient matrices $R^l$ are deterministic Gaussian response coefficients. The primitive reverse group $\zeta^l$ is centered Gaussian with full covariance $S_{l+1}$, independently of the forward groups and roots. These are canonical same-matrix identities, not independent replacements for $A_{l+1}^*$. For explicit dependency checking, their initial coefficients are constructed downwards by


$$
R_{ik}^{(L-1)}=p_k\mathbb E[D_i^LD_k^L]+\mathbf1_{\{i=k\}}\mathbb E[H\phi''(Z_i^L)],\qquad R_{ik}^l=\mathbf1_{\{i=k\}}\mathbb E[\phi''(Z_i^{(l+1)})q_i^{(l+1)}]+R_{ik}^{(l+1)}\mathbb E[D_i^{(l+1)}D_k^{(l+1)}],\quad l<L-1.
$$

These identities follow by differentiating $\beta_i^{l+1}$ in the named $Z_k^{l+1}$ slot with other primitive source groups frozen. They retain both the local current curvature term and the next-layer return. No current response is inverted or discarded.

Conditionally on $Z^l$,


$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\beta^l\mid Z^l)=\operatorname{diag}(D^l)S_{l+1}\operatorname{diag}(D^l)\ge a^2\lambda_{\min}(S_{l+1})I_3.
$$

The return term is measurable in $Z^{l}$ and does not change this conditional covariance. Induction from $S_L>0$ gives $S_l>0$ for every l. In particular


$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\beta^1\mid Z^1)\ge a^2\lambda_{\min}(S_2)I_3.
$$

This remains true when $Z^1$ is singular. It implies


$$
d\|V^1\|_2^2\ge a^2\lambda_{\min}(S_2)\sum_ip_i^2>0,\qquad\|U_j^1\|_2^2\ge a^2\lambda_{\min}(S_2)\sum_i\Gamma_{ji}^2p_i^2\ge a^2\lambda_{\min}(S_2)p_j^2>0.
$$

For every hidden matrix block,


$$
\|V^l\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2=\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{diag}(p)S_l\operatorname{diag}(p)Q_{l-1})>0,\qquad2\le l\le L.
$$

Here $Q_{l-1}$ and $S_l$ are positive definite and $\operatorname{diag}(p)$ is invertible. The trace of the product of two positive definite matrices is positive: conjugating one by the positive square root of the other makes this explicit. Thus all hidden parameter blocks and all bottom samples already have strictly positive direction norm.

#### 4. Every upper sample: a recursive exact return formula {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22656}

For each fixed sample j define deterministic coefficients


$$
c_{ji}^1=\Gamma_{ji}p_i,\qquad c_{ji}^l=p_i(Q_{l-1})_{ij}+c_{ji}^{(l-1)}\mathbb E[D_j^{(l-1)}D_i^{(l-1)}],\quad2\le l\le L.
$$

For $l\ge2$, let $\xi_{t_j^{l-1}}$ be the primitive forward source associated with the added call $A_lt_j^{l-1}$, in the same Gaussian source group as $Z^l$. We claim the exact identity


$$
U_j^l=\xi_{t_j^{(l-1)}}+\sum_ic_{ji}^l\beta_i^l.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666}

At the bottom,


$$
\partial_{\zeta_i^1}t_j^1=D_j^1c_{ji}^1D_i^1.
$$

The same-matrix forward return rule is consequently


$$
A_2t_j^1=\xi_{t_j^1}+\sum_i\beta_i^2c_{ji}^1\mathbb E[D_j^1D_i^1].
$$

Adding $V^2h_j^1=\sum_ip_i(Q_1)_{ij}\beta_i^2$ proves ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) for $l=2$.

Suppose ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) holds at layer $l<L$. Every named $A_l$-forward source is independent of the primitive $A_{l+1}$-reverse group $\zeta^l$. The coefficients in ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) are deterministic. The initialized backward field $\beta_i^l=D_i^l(\zeta_i^l+\sum_kR_{ik}^lh_k^l)$ depends on $\zeta^{l}$ with derivative $D_i^l$. Hence


$$
\partial_{\zeta_i^l}t_j^l=D_j^lc_{ji}^lD_i^l.
$$

The next forward return is exactly


$$
A_{l+1}t_j^l=\xi_{t_j^l}+\sum_i\beta_i^{l+1}c_{ji}^l\mathbb E[D_j^lD_i^l].
$$

Adding the matrix-block contribution $V^{l+1}h_j^l$ proves ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) at layer $l+1$. This establishes ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) through every fixed depth. The second term in $c^l$ is the genuine same-matrix return; omitting it would give a different and incorrect formula.

#### 5. Positive innovations persist through every layer {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22688}

Regress $\xi_{t_j^{l-1}}$ on the three original forward sources $Z^l$ in its own action group. Their covariance is $Q_{l-1}>0$, so this regression has a well-defined independent Gaussian remainder $\epsilon_{l,j}$. Its variance is exactly


$$
\sigma_{l,j}^2=\inf_{b\in\mathbb R^3}\left\|t_j^{(l-1)}-\sum_ib_ih_i^{(l-1)}\right\|_2^2.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22692}

The equality is the covariance rule for forward queries of the same initialized Gaussian action, not an assumption that different calls use different matrices.

For $l=2$ the features $h_i^1$ are measurable with respect to $Z^1$. Therefore ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22692]), conditional variance, and [Section 3](12-three-sample-learning.qmd#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22615) give


$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma_{2,j}^2&\ge\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(t_j^1\mid Z^1)=\mathbb E\left[(D_j^1)^2\sum_{i,k}c_{ji}^1D_i^1(S_2)_{ik}D_k^1c_{jk}^1\right]\\&\ge a^4\lambda_{\min}(S_2)\sum_i\Gamma_{ji}^2p_i^2\ge a^4\lambda_{\min}(S_2)p_j^2>0.\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22698}

The remainder $\epsilon_{2,j}$ is independent of $Z^2$ and the independent reverse group $\zeta^2$ (when $L>2$). Formula ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) expresses all other terms in $U_j^2$ as functions of those reference variables. At $L=2$, $\beta^{2}$ is a function of $Z^{2}$ alone. Thus $\epsilon_{2,j}$ cannot cancel in $U_{j}^{2}$.

Now assume $l\ge2$ and $l<L$. After regression, ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) has the form


$$
U_j^l=\epsilon_{l,j}+F_{l,j}(Z^l,\zeta^l),
$$

where $\epsilon_{l,j}$ is independent of $(Z^l,\zeta^l)$, has variance $\sigma_{l,j}^2$, and $F_{l,j}$ is a measurable function of the displayed reference variables. Consequently


$$
\operatorname{Var}(t_j^l\mid Z^l,\zeta^l)=(D_j^l)^2\sigma_{l,j}^2.
$$

Each $h_i^l$ is measurable in $Z^l$. Applying ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22692]) at layer $l+1$ yields


$$
\sigma_{l+1,j}^2\ge\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(t_j^l\mid Z^l,\zeta^l)=\mathbb E[(D_j^l)^2]\sigma_{l,j}^2\ge a^2\sigma_{l,j}^2>0.
$$ {#eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22716}

Its new Gaussian remainder is independent of $Z^{l+1}$ and $\zeta^{l+1}$, or of $Z^L$ alone at the final layer. Formula ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) again prevents cancellation. This proves $U_j^l\ne0$ for every $j$ and $l=2,\ldots,L$, with the concrete bound


$$
\|U_j^l\|_2^2\ge\sigma_{l,j}^2\ge a^{2l}\lambda_{\min}(S_2)p_j^2>0.
$$

Together with the bottom estimate this covers every sample and layer. Since $D_j^l\ge a$, all feature directions $t_j^l$ are nonzero as well.

Different samples' added forward sources may be correlated; the proof needs only each remainder's independence from the original forward tuple and the separate reverse group. It does not assume that the three added remainders are mutually independent. One may establish the argument in a separate fixed transcript for each j, then include the finite union of those queries on the common canonical space.

#### 6. Why the augmented finite programs and innovations are valid {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22729}

The initialization program has finitely many action calls for fixed L and three samples. Every original backward field has the form of a bounded smooth gate multiplying a finite sum of Gaussian sources and linear-growth functions of Gaussian forward sources. Formula ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22666]) has that form too. All fields appearing in the added queries therefore have every finite moment.

The inputs $t_j^l$ are not asserted to be globally Lipschitz functions of all named sources. To apply the derivative-valid fixed-program theorem, smoothly clip each unbounded incoming factor, use its bounded-derivative finite program, and remove the clips. Canonical action operator bounds give convergence of the actual forward and transpose answers in $L^{2}$. The source derivatives required above are explicitly $D_j^lc_{ji}^lD_i^l$, which are bounded because $\phi'$ is bounded and $c^{l}$ is deterministic. More generally the clipped return terms have integrable finite-source envelopes. Dominated convergence therefore passes the response coefficients. The converging finite covariance Grams identify the joint source limits using continuity of positive semidefinite square roots, without a pseudoinverse-continuity claim.

The positive innovation also follows directly from finite Gaussian conditioning. For the action $A_{l}$, condition on its previous forward calls $A_lV=Y$ and reverse calls $A_l^{\top}U=Q$. The forward inputs V include the three $h_{i}^{l-1}$; the reverse inputs U include the three $\beta_{i}^{l}$. On adding $t=t_j^{l-1}$, the unused Gaussian part of the action answer contains


$$
(\|(I-P_V)t\|_{\mathrm{Euclidean}}/\sqrt n)P_{U^\perp}g_n,
$$

where $g_n$ is an independent standard Gaussian vector. The removed projection has expected normalized squared length $\operatorname{rank}(U)/n$, which tends to zero for this fixed transcript. The residual input norm converges to the strictly positive variance in ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22692]). If other finitely many new queries are included, their joint Gaussian covariance gives the same marginal regression on the original three sources; no assertion that a later query is independent of earlier added queries is needed. This confirms that reuse and transpose conditioning cannot erase the innovation proved in ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22698])--([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l22716]).

Actual adjunction is retained at every step. These are calls of the initialized canonical Gaussian actions and their adjoints, not arbitrary bounded operators substituted for the initialization.

#### 7. Physical acceleration and the exact kernel coefficient {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l22743}

Let a canonical strong physical solution with the strong chain rule be given. Since $C(0)=0$, its predictions vanish and $r_i(0)=-y_i=-3p_i$. The readout equation implies


$$
C'(0)=3H,\qquad C(t)/t\to3H\ \text{in }H_L.
$$

All initial hidden velocities vanish. Bounded multiplication by the gates, strong forward convergence, and operator-norm convergence of the HS action increments give, backward from the top,


$$
b_i^l(t)/t\to3\beta_i^l\ \text{in }H_l.
$$

For completeness, if $D(t)$ are uniformly bounded multipliers converging in probability to $D(0)$ and $q(t)\to q(0)$ in $L^2$, then $D(t)q(t)\to D(0)q(0)$ in $L^2$: split the difference into the multiplier acting on $q(t)-q(0)$ and $(D(t)-D(0))q(0)$, and use dominated convergence on the second. Apply this at each gate, and split each changed action into its fixed initial action and a vanishing operator-norm increment.

Dividing each raw hidden update by t now gives


$$
\theta_h'(t)/t\to9V,\qquad\theta_h(t)=\theta_h(0)+(9/2)t^2V+o_{\mathrm{raw}}(t^2).
$$

The exact strong forward chain rule, applied successively to the L layers, gives


$$
(z_j^l)'(t)/t\to9U_j^l,\qquad(h_j^l)'(t)/t\to9D_j^lU_j^l.
$$

Thus the strong right second derivatives at zero exist and are precisely the stated nonzero accelerations. No second Frechet derivative of the ambient $L^{2}$ Nemytskii map is assumed.

Let J denote the bounded hidden directional linearization of $H(\theta_h)=\sum_ip_ih_i^L$ at initialization. Genuine adjunction gives $J^*H=V$. The preceding chain rule gives


$$
H'(t)/t\to9JV,\qquad H(t)=H+(9/2)t^2JV+o_{L^2}(t^2),\qquad\|H(t)\|_2^2=\|H\|_2^2+9t^2\|V\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}^2+o(t^2).
$$

The hidden part $g_h(t)$ of the raw gradient of $\sum_ip_if_i$ satisfies $g_h(t)/t\to3V$, so


$$
\|g_h(t)\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}^2=9t^2\|V\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}^2+o(t^2).
$$

Finally the exact raw kernel identity is


$$
p^{\top}K_{\mathrm{total}}(t)p=\|g_h(t)\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}^2+\|H(t)\|_2^2.
$$

Adding the two contributions proves the coefficient 18. Because every hidden block is nonzero, $\|V\|_{\mathrm{hidden}}>0$, and the projected total kernel strictly increases from its initial value at all sufficiently small positive physical times. This is the actual kernel along training, with no scalar-clock or permutation argument.

## Uniform fitting of cyclic triples in a fixed-order closure {#sec-fixed-closure-cyclic-triples}

There is a complementary three-sample result for the exact order-one
closure of [the fixed-order model](09-trainability.qmd#sec-fixed-closure-model). Here the activation is fixed as
$\tanh$, the input dimension is three, and the two hidden layers use
@eq-fixed-closure-p1-marks. The conclusion is about this fixed-order
population flow, separately from the dense-network and depth results in
the preceding sections.

::: {#thm-fixed-closure-cyclic-triples}
Let $P$ cyclically permute the three coordinates. For every $u\in S^2$,
train on the equally weighted inputs
$\sqrt3u,\sqrt3Pu,\sqrt3P^2u$, all with target $+1$, from
$(w,c,M)_0=(g,0,D)$. Define the fixed initialized quantity

$$
k_*:=\min_{u\in S^2}\mathbb E_2\left[
 \frac13\sum_{j=0}^2\tanh\{b_2^\top P^jDa_0(u)\}\right]^2.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-cyclic-constant}

Then $k_*>0$, and every such full flow satisfies
$\dot{\mathcal L}\le-4k_*\mathcal L$,
$\mathcal L(t)\le e^{-4k_*t}$, and converges to an actual fitted
endpoint. Bounds on $w-g,c$ in supremum norm and $M$ in Frobenius norm
can be chosen uniformly over $u$. Compatible repeated inputs are included.
Simultaneously negating any subset of the inputs and their labels preserves
all these conclusions and the complete trajectory.
:::

[]{#proof-fixed-closure-cyclic-triples}

::: {.proof}
By @lem-fixed-closure-initial-map,
$z(u):=Da_0(u)=\ell_2(F_0(u_1),F_0(u_2),F_0(u_3))^\top$ is continuous
and nonzero on the unit sphere, and $z(P^ju)=P^jz(u)$.
For any nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^3$ put
$\ell_j(b)=b^\top P^jz$. The analytic function
$U_z(b)=\frac13\sum_{j=0}^2\tanh\ell_j(b)$ is not identically zero
near $b=0$. If $z_1+z_2+z_3\ne0$, its linear Taylor term is nonzero.
Otherwise $\ell_0+\ell_1+\ell_2=0$, so

$$
\ell_0^3+\ell_1^3+\ell_2^3=3\ell_0\ell_1\ell_2\not\equiv0.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-cyclic-cubic}

Each linear factor is nonzero because $P^jz\ne0$, and a product of
nonzero polynomials is nonzero. Since
$\tanh t=t-t^3/3+O(t^5)$, the cubic term is nonzero in this case.
Positive upper density on the open cube then gives
$\mathbb E_2U_{z(u)}(b_2)^2>0$ for every $u$. This expectation is
continuous in $u$ by dominated convergence, using $|U_z|\le1$.
Compactness of $S^2$ proves that the minimum in
@eq-fixed-closure-cyclic-constant is strictly positive.

To verify the dynamical symmetry, let $S_1$ and $S_2$ permute their
respective Gaussian coordinates by $P$, and set
$P_1=\operatorname{diag}(P,P)$. Then
$b_1\circ S_1=P_1b_1$, $b_2\circ S_2=Pb_2$ and
$PD=DP_1$. The isometry

$$
(w,c,M)\longmapsto
(P^\top w\circ S_1,c\circ S_2,P^\top MP_1)
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-cyclic-isometry}

fixes initialization and sends $f(v)$ to $f(Pv)$, as direct changes of
variables in the two populations verify. The equally weighted data loss
and $F=\frac13\sum_{j=0}^2f(P^ju)$ are invariant. Uniqueness therefore
keeps all three predictions equal along both the initialized ascent and
physical flows. With
$U=\frac13\sum_jH^{(2)}(P^ju)$, the exact full physical equation is
$\dot X=2(1-F)\nabla F$. The initialized number
$C_0=\mathbb E_2U_0^2$ is at least $k_*$.
Apply @lem-fixed-closure-scalar-clock to obtain the stated rate and an
endpoint at ascent time $s_*\le1/k_*$. The bounds
@eq-fixed-closure-ascent-bounds are uniform because the feature envelopes,
$D$, and this upper bound on $s_*$ do not depend on $u$.

Finally $f(-v)=-f(v)$ at every state. Negating a labeled pair $(v,y)$
changes its residual to its negative and its prediction gradient to its
negative, so the loss and every parameter velocity remain unchanged.
This proves the last assertion without introducing another symmetry
assumption.
:::

For a concrete range of geometries put

$$
u_\theta=\cos\theta\frac{(1,1,1)}{\sqrt3}
 +\sin\theta\frac{(2,-1,-1)}{\sqrt6},\qquad
0\le\theta\le\pi/2.
$$ {#eq-fixed-closure-cyclic-opening}

The normalized input Gram of $u_\theta,Pu_\theta,P^2u_\theta$ has
eigenvalues $3\cos^2\theta$ and $\tfrac32\sin^2\theta$ twice.
Indeed the common coordinate direction contributes the rank-one
$\cos^2\theta$ matrix, while the three planar components sum to zero,
have unit lengths and pairwise inner products $-1/2$. Every interior
triple is independent; the first endpoint has three equal inputs and the
second is a planar $120$-degree triple. The same $k_*$ works throughout.
At the planar endpoint, negate the last input and label. Then
$x_3=x_1+x_2$, the labels are $(1,1,-1)$, and the label-weighted first
input moment is zero. A homogeneous linear predictor fitting the first
two labels would give value two at $x_3$, whereas the initialized nonlinear
closure fits all three. This comparison is with homogeneous linear
predictors. The mixed label masses are $2/3$ and $1/3$; no stability
under arbitrary rotations, unequal weights or independent perturbations
is asserted.

## Scope of the completed families {#sec-docs-special-data-limits-l27238}

The full-limit proofs in Parts I–III retain actual Gaussian initialization, the trained operator
and its transpose, raw GD and the loss clocks stated above. Caps and Gaussian
query perturbations are proof devices removed in the indicated order.
No result asserts a joint growing-depth/width limit, a generalization theorem,
or convergence of finite-optimizer infinite-time endpoints.

Part I proves $f_2=-f_1$ and $0<f_1(t)<1$ for every $t>0$.
Its formula ([-@eq-docs-special-data-limits-l1751]) does not prove that the integrated kernel diverges;
therefore asymptotic fitting is not included for that family.
Part II proves fitting for equal labels at every fixed admissible angle,
not global opposite-label $L=3$ dynamics. Part III proves persistent
nonaffinity and nonzero initial acceleration, not strictly positive
velocity at every later positive time. Its large-gain construction is
not a claim of a depth-uniform *relative* nonlinear effect.

The three-sample common-gain classes and depth-uniform absolute margins
have exactly the quantifiers in III.A. Sharing an activation or a gain
across a class does not assert uniform finite-width convergence over that
class. No coefficient expansion, total-positivity premise or unproved
long-transcript Gaussian theorem is used.

Part IV is a distinct partial result for actual correlated-data dynamics.
Its strong first-layer topology retains kinetic energy and the complete
residual-weighted first-kernel matrix along converging subsequences, including
off-diagonal entries. It proves neither a common GF/GD subsequential limit nor
an autonomous population equation, full-sequence convergence, or unweighted
kernel convergence. Its two endpoint conventions and raw-row reconstruction
are stated in that part; no global-limit conclusion is inferred from compactness.

Part V concerns initialized geometry only. Absolute and variance-normalized
sample conditioning, and scalar affine-regression residuals, are different
quantities. Its calibrated depth limit is sequential after width, with a
depth-dependent activation; none of its Gaussian recursions is asserted for
trained non-Gaussian fields. These comparisons neither extend Parts I–III nor
turn their absolute nonaffinity into a depth-uniform relative margin.
